A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GazeGaussian and contain readable text, equations, tables, and figures. Corresponding main-text material can be matched reliably. The supplied v1 ends with references; v2 additionally includes supplementary Sections 7–13.

before.justification: v1 reports original gaze-redirection experiments across four datasets, quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–2, and component ablations in Table 3.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and additionally reports downstream gaze-estimation results, cross-dataset ablations, renderer-enhanced baseline comparisons, and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The two-stream architecture, eye rotation, expression-guided renderer, and training losses are retained. A localized specification change appears in the gaze-conditioned eye-color MLP: its input changes from Gaussian positions X0e in v1 Equation 7 to Gaussian features z0e in v2 Equation 5. The PDFs do not establish whether this reflects an implementation change or a correction to the written formula.

E1.justification: ETH-XGaze, ColumbiaGaze, MPIIFaceGaze, and GazeCapture remain the dataset coverage. v2 adds actual evaluation of downstream few-shot gaze-estimator personalization in Section 5.5 and an identity-interpolation demonstration in Section 12.2. v1 mentions the downstream benefit but supplies no corresponding results.

E2.justification: The original comparison methods remain in Tables 1–2. v2 substantially expands the controls with GazeNeRF+EGNR and Gaussian Head Avatar+EGNR in Table 5, testing whether the proposed renderer explains the advantage. Figure 6 includes real-only estimator fine-tuning, while Table 6 adds Wang et al. using explicitly attributed published scores rather than a reproduced experiment.

E3.justification: The existing redirection protocols retain the 14.4K-image training subset, evaluation pairings, resolution, and metrics. New Section 5.5 evaluates estimator fine-tuning with one to nine real calibration images and fixes augmented training sets at 200 real-plus-generated samples. Newly disclosed epoch counts and preprocessing parameters describe existing experiments rather than establish changed settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds cross-dataset component ablations in Table 4 and renderer-transfer controls in Table 5, extending the original within-dataset ablation. Sections 12–13 also add transformed-Gaussian inspection, identity interpolation with fixed gaze and pose, expanded qualitative ablations, and an illustrated accessory-reconstruction failure case.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new gaze-estimation curves in Figure 6 show point estimates without uncertainty bands or error bars.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their numerical results. Table 3 changes identity similarity without eye rotation from 38.521 to 41.521. v2 adds downstream error curves, cross-dataset ablation scores, renderer-control results, and qualitative findings. Figure 6 places GazeGaussian augmentation lowest in error throughout. New Table 5 also gives Gaussian Head Avatar head error as 8.498, inconsistently with 13.563 in retained Table 1.

T1.justification: v2 Section 4.1 adds explicit covariance, Gaussian-kernel, and alpha-compositing definitions where v1 primarily listed Gaussian attributes and used a rasterization operator. Most subsequent mathematics is retained under renamed notation and consolidated equations, with localized formula corrections. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain first integration of 3DGS into gaze redirection, explicit eye rotation, separate face/eye modeling, expression-guided generalization, and strong performance across four datasets. Subject-specific conditioning receives greater emphasis, and downstream usefulness receives new evidence, but these do not establish a new overarching contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explains EGNR more explicitly through subject-specific information and identity preservation, and discusses why adding it to existing baselines leaves representation limitations. Section 13 newly identifies tracking-related difficulties with glasses, earrings, and hair, supported by Figure 9. These qualify applicability without overturning the original interpretation.

D1.justification: New Sections 9–10 disclose Adam optimization, a 1e-4 initial learning rate with exponential decay, 10 initialization epochs plus 20 pipeline epochs, NVIDIA 4090 hardware, 680 mm normalization, and single-image adaptation timing. They distinguish the VGG-based loss estimator from ResNet50 evaluation. v2 also clarifies Gaussian Head Avatar conditioning and changes the code statement from future release to claimed availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Adam and GaussianHair and sharpens discussion of Gaussian Head Avatar's single-avatar scope. Wang et al., already cited in v1, gains a quantitative literature comparison. The main related-work coverage remains; consolidating Gaussian Head Avatar's preprint/publication references does not remove a distinct work.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the method exposition, replaces notation throughout, and consolidates separate attribute descriptions into grouped equations. It introduces a numbered section/subsection hierarchy, revises explanatory passages across the abstract and experiments, and incorporates an organized supplementary narrative. This extends beyond isolated language corrections.

P2.justification: v2 retains the original core figures but redistributes comparison figures and tables within a revised typographic layout. It adds Figure 6, Tables 4–6, and Figures 7–13, covering downstream performance, controls, Gaussian geometry, identity morphing, failures, and expanded visual comparisons. These substantially expand and reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves evidential support and reproducibility: Section 5.5 supplies results for a downstream benefit previously asserted without supporting outcomes, Tables 4–5 strengthen component attribution and generalization evidence, and Sections 9–10 disclose essential implementation details. The illustrated limitations also improve transparency. These gains outweigh localized inconsistencies, including Gaussian Head Avatar's conflicting head-error entries and the unexplained relationship between 74 FPS and 0.2 seconds per generated image.
